feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so no outcome is claimed for it. Evidence: iteration 3 (y=0.07 m, ±0.05 m spread, 16 mm, wheel_radius 0.03 m, 51.31) had the best s-bend progress (0.155) but one line-loss event per run on s-bend and slalom, with slalom max_error 0.065 m. Iteration 6 (wheel_radius 0.04 m, 47.71) showed that higher ground speed also brings back line loss and cuts s-bend progress to 0.1325, so speed should stay at 0.03 m. Iteration 4 (y=0.06 m) and iteration 5 (y=0.05 m) show that the lead below 0.07 m loses most of the s-bend gain. Slalom steering_oscillation stayed near 0.14 at every row tested, so the row position is not its cause. The oval has been fixed at progress 0.1125 and max_error about 0.060 m since iteration 1. What I had to compensate for: I kept kp 2.0, kd 0.10 and ki 0, and kept the weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] matched to the spread, so the signal stays about ±2 on the wider spread. Next race: if line_loss_events return on s-bend or slalom at y=0.065 m, the lead is still too aggressive for this speed; return to y=0.07 m and keep the ±0.065 m spread. If slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with zero line loss, widen the spread toward ±0.08 m (the maximum allowed) with 16 mm footprints. If steering_oscillation stays above 0.10 on slalom with zero line loss, geometry is not the lever, so I will change the controller, not the geometry.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events return on s-bend or slalom at sensor y=0.065 m (iteration 3 had one per run at y=0.07 m), return sensor y to 0.07 m and keep the ±0.065 m spread, to test whether the lead is what causes the loss.

If slalom max_error stays at or above 0.06 m with zero line loss (iteration 3 gave 0.065 m at ±0.05 m), widen sensor x to ±0.08 m with sensor_size 0.016 m, so the line stays under the sensors at the largest bend offsets.

If the score is at or above 51.3 with zero line loss, keep geometry fixed and try sensor_size 0.012 m at ±0.065 m, to test whether a smaller footprint reduces the signal jitter that the 16 mm footprint may add (iteration 6 showed speed is not the lever).
